body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: e973bfd3bcb03d8192a9d9753deda3ce536aa1e6 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge**, after its parents #800 and #805. This review covers only e973bfd3, the commit on top of #805's head 279e1780.

### What looks good
- **Collision envelopes are on the safe side where it counts.**
  - The collar is Ø38.1 mm, above both nuts (Ø35 / Ø32).
  - The set-screw body is drawn at r 20.05, wider than the collar. The photo on page 4 of the TTS manual shows the real set-screw body narrower than its collar.
  - Both ER nuts come from the one ER table and are never under Tormach's published Ø34 / Ø27.
  - `the_tts_er20_collar_strikes_a_wall_its_nut_misses` proves through the real fixture gate that the collar is swept.
- **Gauge-line semantics match the BT/CAT entries.** Every profile tops out at the spindle's reference plane:
  - BT/CAT stop at the taper gauge line, above the flange by the standoff.
  - TTS stops at the collar face, which the manual says seats on the spindle face and is the surface tools are measured from (page 2 "Principles of Operation", page 5 "Tool Measurement").
  - Posting does not read the holder gauge (H offsets come from the machine's tool table). The collision path reads the drawn profile and `judged` (`holder_len` 52, `holder_d` 38.1), the same way it does for BT/CAT.
- **`Taper` change is safe:**
  - `points()` (crates/tools/src/holder_library.rs:267-272) gives the same output as before when `standoff > 0`, and every BT30/BT40/CAT40 constant has a non-zero standoff. The existing point-by-point BT/CAT tests still pass unchanged.
  - `ring` is display-only. `Taper` has no serde derive and is never saved: an applied holder is stored as drawn points. Old project files are not affected, and `project_roundtrip` passes (71/71).
  - The zero-standoff profile stays closed and revolvable. This is pinned by `every_tts_profile_is_closed_and_tops_out_at_the_collar_face` at the default, a long and the minimum gauge.
- **Sources:** dimensions and part numbers only, with URLs in `docs/decisions/794-tts-holders.md`. No Tormach text or models are copied (the solid-models forum thread is cited for file names only).
- **The premise correction is consistent.** The diff says only that the 770MX/1100MX are BT30, and the machine default is filed as #828 (open). Nothing claims the 770MX uses TTS. The ER20 outline test's doc comment names the 770M / 1100M, which is correct.
- **Laws:**
  - no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests;
  - the new module has its provenance header, and every touched file is under 400 lines (`holder_library.rs` 357);
  - no snapshot PNGs, build.rs, scripts, `.github` or dependency changes;
  - the body has a `Changelog:` line and ends `Fixes #794`.

### Local results (worktree merged with current upstream main: clean, no conflicts; macOS, debug, private target)
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `camcraft-tools --lib holder_library` | 12 passed |
| app `--test holder_library` | 11 passed |
| app `--test project_roundtrip` | 71 passed |
| app `--test tool_body` | 8 passed |
| app `--test tool_spun_profile` | 7 passed |
| ui `--lib tool_holder` (CWD crates/ui) | 5 passed |
| ui `--lib structural` (CWD crates/ui) | 4 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **Collar thickness is a guess, not a proven upper bound.**
   - Where: `crates/tools/src/holder_library_tts.rs:30`, 0.5 in.
   - The risk: if a real collar is thicker than 12.7 mm, the band just below it is drawn on the ER holders at the Ø35 body plus the 45° flare instead of at Ø38.1. That would under-envelope by up to 1.55 mm radially in that band. The set-screw holders are not affected: their body is wider than the collar.
   - The manual's ER20 photo (page 4) shows a collar visibly thinner than the 19.5 mm nut, so 12.7 is probably on the safe side. The measurement request in the PR body covers it; worth confirming when a TTS user measures.
2. **ER16 nut, Ø32 against the published Ø27.** This is a 2.5 mm radial over-envelope.
   - It is safe, and keeping one ER table is a reasonable trade.
   - The cost: false holder hits in tight pockets for TTS ER16 users. The workaround (edit the landed Custom profile) is in the decision file.
   - A per-holder nut override would be a cheap follow-up if users report false hits.
3. **Set-screw default gauge, 60 mm.** It comes from the blank's machinable length, so it is plausibly at or above the real installed height. A longer default is the safe direction: the drawn body and collar reach at least as high as the real steel. It is still unpublished.
4. **`Fixes #794` closes the issue with two of its "Done means" not met.**
   - The 770MX default moved to #828.
   - "Checked on the user's 770MX" cannot happen, because that machine is BT30.
   - Both are explained in the PR and decision file. The maintainer may want a short comment on #794 recording the premise correction when it closes.
5. **Stacked:** this merges after #805 and #800 (retarget/merge order per AGENTS.md "Overlapping issues stack"). The PR's base is already `main`.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
